newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy parlt approves move of FS debt to state.
newsitem.headline: Italy parlt approves move of FS debt to state.

text.p: Italy's Chamber of Deputies (lower house) approved a government measure within the 1997 budget law which will convert national railway Ferrovie dello Stato (FS) state loans into a form of direct state debt, reducing the burden on state accounts.
The measure passed, article 28, is part of 12.5 trillion lire worth of so-called Treasury operations within the budget which aims to lop 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit.
Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has said at least half the Treasury operations will come from lower expenditure on public debt.

Treasury undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta told reporters that every year the state transfers around 8.0 trillion lire to settle FS debt, comprising 5.0 trillion in interest and 3.0 trillion in capital.
The new measure will allow the conversion of the 3.0 trillion lire into a form of state equity stake or capital increase in FS, thus reducing the burden on the state accounts by the same amount.
FS posted 1995 group losses of 1.57 trillion lire against 1994 losses of 2.65 trillion lire.
The lower house is examining and voting on the draft budget law article by article and has until November 14 to ratify the package which then passes to the upper house Senate.
